_request.system:
You classify a single ERP requirement into exactly one of four delivery tiers, using only the SAP standard-process knowledge entries provided to you.

  Fit           The delivered standard already does this once baseline org structures exist.
  Configuration The delivered logic does this, driven by values maintained in customizing                 (thresholds, code lists, org units, number ranges, determination rules). No code.
  Enhancement   The standard process still drives the flow, but a delivered object must carry an                 extra custom field, or extra logic must run at a published extension point.
  Development   The standard provides no object, no process, and no extension point covering the                 request; a new program, interface, or persistence must be built and maintained.

Method:
- Reason from the knowledge entries' stated boundaries: what the standard covers, what is a   configuration point, and what is stated to be beyond the standard.
- Do NOT classify from surface features. "It mentions an external system" is not a reason.   The reason must be that the standard provides no object, process, or extension point for it,   and that the transport, mapping, scheduling, and error handling are project deliverables.
- A requirement to make an already-delivered field required is field-status configuration.   A requirement to enforce entry in a field the delivered object does not have, or to gate a   process on a condition the standard data model does not carry, is an enhancement.
- In rationale, cite the specific entry IDs whose boundary decided the call, and say what that   boundary is. Cite only entries you were given.
- Set confidence below 0.7 when the entries conflict or none of them squarely covers the request.
_request.user:
Requirement (R2R): Send a nightly custom file to the Auralis Separation Ledger with Day-1 balances for treasury reconciliation outside the ERP during the first two quarters.

Verbatim from the workshop: "the reporting analyst asked for a nightly custom file to be sent to the fictional Auralis Separation Ledger, because the treasury separation team uses it to reconcile Day-1 balances outside the ERP for the first two quarters."

Knowledge entries retrieved for this requirement:

### KB-R2R-004 — Financial reporting, extraction, and reconciliation feeds [R2R]
Standard process: Financial data is exposed for reporting through delivered analytical views and released APIs, and standard reports and statements are produced from the ledger without any build. What is not delivered is a recurring file whose layout, naming, delivery window, and reconciliation semantics are dictated by a receiving application. Producing such a file means selecting and aggregating the data, formatting it to the receiving system's contract, scheduling the job, handling partial and failed runs, and providing the audit trail that shows what was sent and when. The ledger data itself is standard; the feed is a build.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Delivered analytical views over the ledger and released APIs for extraction.; Standard financial statements, trial balance, and line item reports.; Reconciliation between subledgers and the general ledger.; Scheduling framework for delivered background jobs.
Common configuration points: Financial statement versions and report variants.; Job scheduling for delivered close activities.
Typically beyond the standard: A nightly file in a layout defined by an external ledger or consolidation tool.; Reconciliation logic that compares ERP balances against balances held outside the ERP system.

### KB-R2R-001 — Record-to-report end-to-end standard flow [R2R]
Standard process: Financial accounting posts journal entries to the general ledger, either automatically from operational documents or manually. Documents carry a document type, a posting date, and a period, and the delivered period control decides whether a period is open for a given account type. Open items on customer, supplier, and general ledger accounts are cleared against each other. Period close runs recurring entries, accruals, revaluation, and reconciliation, and financial statements are produced from a financial statement version that arranges accounts into the required hierarchy. Running the ledger, posting journals, closing periods, clearing open items, and producing statements is delivered behaviour.
Capabilities covered by the standard: General ledger posting from operational documents and manual journals.; Open item management and automatic clearing.; Period open and close control per account type and per company code.; Financial statement versions and the reports built on them.; Parallel ledgers and currencies.
Common configuration points: Document types and their number ranges.; Posting period variants and which periods are open for which account types.; Automatic clearing rules and tolerance groups.; Financial statement version hierarchies.
Typically beyond the standard: Statement structures that the financial statement version cannot express.; Recurring bespoke extracts whose layout is defined by a receiving system.

### KB-XC-002 — Integration with non-SAP, legacy, and third-party systems [cross_cutting]
Standard process: The ERP publishes released APIs and message interfaces for its business objects, and these are part of the delivered standard. What the standard does not deliver is the interface itself. A project-specific connection to a named external application always has to be built: somebody must design the payload mapping, decide the trigger and schedule, implement error handling and retry, provide monitoring and reprocessing, and own the interface for its lifetime. This remains true even when both endpoints are entirely standard and even when the data being moved is standard data. Recurring extracts, nightly file drops, spreadsheet imports, portal order intake, and pushes into an external ledger or archive all share this property: the transport, the mapping, and the operational surface are project deliverables, not shipped content.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Released OData and A2X services for reading and writing master data and documents.; Message-based interfaces for common document exchange patterns.; Standard inbound processing for widely adopted electronic document formats.; Application logs and monitoring for delivered interface frameworks.
Common configuration points: Communication arrangements, partner profiles, and endpoint destinations.; Message types and their assignment to partners.; Output determination that decides when a document triggers an outbound message.
Typically beyond the standard: Any bespoke interface to a specifically named external or legacy application.; Scheduled extracts whose file layout is defined by the receiving system.; Converting an external portal's payload into ERP documents when the payload is not a standard format.; Importing values maintained in an external spreadsheet or archive into ERP records.

### KB-P2P-001 — Procure-to-pay end-to-end standard flow [P2P]
Standard process: The delivered procurement flow begins with a purchase requisition that captures demand, either entered manually or generated by material requirements planning. The requisition is converted into a purchase order against a supplier and, where one exists, a source of supply such as a contract or info record. Goods receipt records the physical arrival and posts inventory and a goods-receipt/invoice-receipt clearing entry. Supplier invoice verification matches the invoice against the purchase order and the goods receipt, applying tolerance checks, and releases the invoice for payment. The three-way match between order, receipt, and invoice is delivered behaviour and does not need to be built.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Purchase requisition creation, conversion, and item categories.; Purchase order with header and item data, delivery schedules, and account assignment.; Goods receipt posting with movement types and inventory update.; Supplier invoice verification with three-way match and tolerance handling.; Payment proposal and outgoing payment processing.
Common configuration points: Document types for requisitions and purchase orders.; Tolerance keys and limits for price and quantity variance at invoice verification.; Account determination for goods receipt and invoice receipt postings.; Purchasing groups and purchasing organizations and their assignments.
Typically beyond the standard: Replacing the three-way match with a different matching rule.; Feeding requisitions or orders to an application outside the ERP system on a schedule.

parsed.rationale: The requirement is to build a recurring custom file for an external system (Auralis Separation Ledger) with a specific layout for Day-1 balances. According to KB-R2R-004, a nightly file whose layout, naming, and delivery are dictated by a receiving application is not delivered; producing it is a build. KB-XC-002 states that any bespoke interface to a named external application is a project deliverable, including scheduled extracts with custom formats. KB-R2R-001 lists recurring bespoke extracts as beyond the standard. The standard provides no object, process, or extension point for this end-to-end feed; therefore, it requires development.
